title: A Study to Investigate the Long-term Safety and Efficacy of Belimumab in Adults With Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) Associated With Systemic Sclerosis (SSc) and Other Connective Tissue Diseases (CTD) (BLISSconneCTD-OLE)
off: An Open Label Study to Investigate the Long-term Safety and Efficacy of Belimumab in Adults With Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD) Associated With Systemic Sclerosis (SSc) and Other Connective Tissue Diseases (CTD)
summary: This is an open label extension (OLE) study of an ongoing randomized controlled parent clinical studies 218224 (NCT05878717) and 221672 (NCT06572384) which aim to assess the efficacy and safety of belimumab on reducing the decline in lung function in participants with interstitial lung disease associated with diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis (dcSSc-ILD) and interstitial lung disease associated with other connective tissue diseases (CTD-ILD), respectively. The OLE study will describe how well tolerated belimumab will be long term, and whether it might continue to slow progression of lung function decline, slow overall disease progression and improve quality of life.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participants with SSc-ILD or other CTD-ILDs that have completed either study 218224 or 221672 through to and including the Week 52 visit and are not considered treatment failure, defined as meeting either of the following criteria:

  * Discontinuation of study medication during study 218224 or 221672 for any reason.
* Participants with SSc should have an area of uninvolved or mildly thickened skin that, in the opinion of the investigator, would allow subcutaneous (SC) injection at the abdomen or the front, middle region of the thigh.
* Participant is capable and willing to self-administer the study medication or has a caregiver/healthcare professional who is capable and willing to administer the study medication throughout the study.
* Female participants: A female participant is eligible to participate if she is not pregnant or breastfeeding, and one of the following conditions applies:

Is a woman of non-childbearing potential (WONCBP) or is a woman of childbearing potential (WOCBP) and using a contraceptive method that is highly effective, with a failure rate of less than (\<)1 percentage (%), during the study treatment period and for at least 4 months after the last dose of study intervention. The investigator should evaluate potential for contraceptive method failure (e.g., non-compliance, recently initiated) in relationship to the first dose of study intervention.

1. A WOCBP must have a negative highly sensitive pregnancy test (urine or serum, as required by local regulations) within 24 hours before the first dose of study intervention.
2. If a urine test cannot be confirmed as negative (e.g., an ambiguous result), a serum pregnancy test is required. In such cases, the participant must be excluded from participation if the serum pregnancy result is positive.
3. Additional requirements for pregnancy testing during and after study intervention are located.
4. The investigator is responsible for review of medical history, menstrual history, and recent sexual activity to decrease the risk for inclusion of a woman with an early undetected pregnancy.

   * Capable of giving signed informed consent which includes compliance with the requirements and restrictions listed in the informed consent form (ICF) and in the protocol.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Participants of study 218224 or study 221672 who have discontinued study treatment, prior to Week 52.
* Participants who have developed clinical evidence of significant, unstable or uncontrolled, acute or chronic diseases not due to SSc or other CTD (i.e, cardiovascular, pulmonary, hematologic, gastrointestinal, hepatic, renal, neurological, malignancy or infectious diseases), or experienced an AE in study 218224 or study 221672 that could, in the opinion of the principal investigator, put the participant at undue risk.
* Participants who have developed any other medical diseases (eg, cardiopulmonary), laboratory abnormalities, or conditions (eg, poor venous access) that, in the opinion of the investigator could significantly alter the absorption, metabolism, or elimination of drugs; constitutes a risk when taking the study intervention; interferes with the interpretation of data; or it is not safe for the participant to continue on the study.
* Participants who have been exposed to ionizing radiation in excess of 10 millisievert (mSv) above background over the previous 3 year period as a result of occupational exposure or previous participation in research studies.
* QT Interval Corrected (QTc) greater than (\>) 480 millisecond (msec) at Week 52 of parent study 218224 or study 221672.

primary.m: Number of participants with Adverse events (AEs), Adverse Event of Special Interest events (AESIs), and Serious Adverse Event (SAEs)

x.titre: Extension en ouvert du bélimumab dans les PID associées à la sclérodermie et aux autres connectivites
x.question: Le bélimumab est-il bien toléré et reste-t-il efficace à long terme chez les patients atteints de PID associée à une sclérodermie ou à une autre connectivite ?
x.contexte:
Les pneumopathies interstitielles diffuses (PID) associées aux connectivites, en particulier à la sclérodermie systémique, exposent à un déclin progressif de la fonction respiratoire. Les traitements disponibles ralentissent la progression sans l'arrêter, et les données de tolérance à long terme des biothérapies dans ces indications sont limitées.

Cette étude est l'extension en ouvert de deux essais randomisés en cours de phase 2/3 : l'un dans la PID de la sclérodermie diffuse (NCT05878717) et l'autre dans les PID des autres connectivites (NCT06572384). Les participants ayant terminé la semaine 52 sans échec thérapeutique reçoivent le bélimumab, un anticorps anti-BAFF, sans placebo. L'étude décrit la tolérance au long cours et explore si le médicament continue de freiner le déclin de la fonction pulmonaire, la progression globale de la maladie et la qualité de vie. Le promoteur est GlaxoSmithKline, avec 514 participants prévus.
x.interet: Cette extension apportera des données de sécurité sur plusieurs années, indispensables avant tout usage chronique du bélimumab dans ces PID. Elle donnera aussi une première idée de la durabilité de l'effet, sans comparateur.
x.profil: Des adultes atteints de PID associée à une sclérodermie ou à une autre connectivite, ayant terminé 52 semaines d'un des essais parents.
inclusion: Fin de l'essai parent (218224 ou 221672) jusqu'à la semaine 52 incluse, sans échec thérapeutique
Sclérodermie : zone de peau saine ou peu épaissie permettant l'injection sous-cutanée
Capacité à s'injecter le traitement (ou aidant disponible)
Contraception efficace pour les femmes en âge de procréer, test de grossesse négatif
exclusion: Arrêt du traitement de l'essai parent avant la semaine 52
Maladie aiguë ou chronique instable non liée à la connectivite (cardiovasculaire, pulmonaire, hépatique, rénale, cancer, infection, etc.)
Événement indésirable dans l'essai parent exposant à un risque excessif
Anomalie ou affection pouvant modifier le métabolisme du médicament ou rendre la poursuite risquée
Exposition aux rayonnements ionisants > 10 mSv sur 3 ans
QTc > 480 ms à la semaine 52 de l'essai parent

bras.traitement: Bélimumab en ouvert (dose et rythme non précisés)

x.critere: Nombre de participants avec événements indésirables, événements d'intérêt particulier et événements indésirables graves, sur environ 5 ans
